result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.common_neighbor_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Score node pairs for link prediction with Common Neighbor and Centrality (CCPA). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.common_neighbor_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Score node pairs for link prediction with Common Neighbor and Centrality (CCPA). title: >- [Graph.common_neighbor_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Score node pairs for link prediction with Common Neighbor and Centrality (CCPA). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Score node pairs for link prediction with Common Neighbor and Centrality (CCPA). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L28583-L28645){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.common_neighbor_centrality( ebunch=None, alpha=0.8, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Common neighbor centrality](../assets/graphs/common-neighbor-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A path A, B, C, D. The candidate link A–C (dashed) joins nodes that share the neighbor B (accent) and are 2 steps apart. With alpha 0.8 and 4 nodes, the table scores every non-adjacent pair as 0.8 times the shared neighbors plus 0.2 times 4 over the distance: A–C and B–D score 1.2, and A–D, with no shared neighbor and 3 steps apart, only 0.267." width="100%"} CCPA (Ahmad et al., 2020) combines two signals that a missing link should exist: how many neighbors the two nodes share, and how close they are. For nodes `u` and `v` the score is $$\alpha \, |N(u) \cap N(v)| + (1 - \alpha) \frac{n}{d(u, v)},$$ where $n$ is the number of nodes and $d$ the shortest-path distance (pairs in different components get no distance bonus). It improves on plain common-neighbor counts for pairs that share no neighbors yet sit close together. With `alpha=1` it is exactly the number of common neighbors. The graph is treated as undirected and simple (parallel edges count once). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ebunch]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of `(u, v)` pairs to score (IDs or labels). If `None` (default), every pair of non-adjacent nodes is scored. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.8]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The weight of the common-neighbor term, between 0 and 1 (default 0.8). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(u, v, score)` triples with node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, a node does not exist, or a pair repeats a node. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Common neighbors are counted by set intersection and distances by breadth-first search, run once per distinct source node in the pairs, so scoring all pairs costs $O(V(V + E))$. The scores match NetworkX's `common_neighbor_centrality`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a path A-B-C-D, the pair A-C shares the neighbor B and is two steps apart, so it scores higher than A-D, which shares nothing and is three steps apart: ::: {#8828e9d8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) [(g.get_label_from_id(u), g.get_label_from_id(v), round(s, 2)) for u, v, s in g.common_neighbor_centrality()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('A', 'C', 1.2), ('A', 'D', 0.27), ('B', 'D', 1.2)] ``` ::: :::
